title: CSS Syntax, Selectors, and Application
description: Dive deeper into CSS syntax, different types of selectors, and how CSS rules are applied to HTML elements.

lessons.title: CSS Rule Structure Recap
lessons.content: A CSS rule consists of a selector and a declaration block. The declaration block contains property-value pairs that define how the selected elements should be styled.

lessons.title: Element, Class, and ID Selectors
Descendant and Child Selectors
Adjacent and General Sibling Selectors
Specificity and Inheritance
lessons.content: CSS applies rules based on specificity: Inline > ID > Class > Element. Some properties like `color` and `font-family` are inherited by default.

lessons.title: Important Rule and Best Practices
lessons.content: The `!important` declaration overrides all other rules, but should be used sparingly. Organize selectors clearly and avoid overly specific rules to maintain flexibility.
